Academic Profile

Program Overview

The undergraduate business administration program, referred to as BBA/BSBA in departmental documentation, provides a broad foundation in business and management. It develops students' understanding of organizational functions, business environments, decision-making, and entrepreneurial opportunities. The curriculum covers major areas such as: • Principles of Management and Organizational Behavior • Accounting, Finance, and Economics • Marketing and Consumer Behavior • Human Resource Management • Business Statistics and Research Methods • Business Law and Taxation • Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management • International Business and E-Commerce • Management Information Systems • Corporate Ethics and Social Responsibility • Research Projects and relevant professional courses The program emphasizes practical application through projects, presentations, research activities, internships, and other learning opportunities in accordance with the approved scheme of studies.

Eligibility Criteria

Intermediate (FA / F.Sc / I.Com / ICS) or equivalent 12-year qualification with at least 45% marks from an accredited Board/Institution. Candidates possessing equivalent qualifications must provide an IBCC equivalence certificate. Admission is subject to the University's merit, admission test, and statutory admission criteria.

Admission Test

University of Loralai requires eligible applicants to appear in an admission test conducted by the University or present a valid national testing score. Final admission is determined strictly on academic merit.

Specialized Tracks

Students select specialized elective clusters in final semesters:

  • Human Resource Management (HRM)
  • Finance & Banking
  • Marketing

Career Prospects

  • Banking & Financial Institutions (Commercial, Islamic & Microfinance)
  • Marketing, Brand Management & Sales Operations
  • Human Resource Management (HRM) & Talent Development
  • Business Development & Strategic Planning
  • Corporate Administration & Operations Management
  • Management Consultancy & Advisory Services
  • Entrepreneurship & Small Business Management
  • Public Sector Organizations & Civil Services (CSS / PMS)
  • Academic Teaching & Management Research
  • Postgraduate Studies (MS Management Sciences, MBA, and PhD Pathways)

Graduate Competencies

Program Learning Outcomes (PLOs)

7 Learning Outcomes
PLO 1

Business and Management Knowledge

Apply relevant management theories, principles, and practices to organizational situations.

PLO 2

Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving

Analyse business and managerial problems and develop appropriate solutions.

PLO 3

Research and Analytical Skills

Apply suitable research methods and analytical techniques to investigate management-related issues.

PLO 4

Communication and Collaboration

Communicate effectively and work collaboratively in academic and professional environments.

PLO 5

Ethics and Social Responsibility

Demonstrate ethical conduct and evaluate the social and environmental implications of decisions.

PLO 6

Leadership and Entrepreneurship

Demonstrate leadership, initiative, and entrepreneurial capabilities.

PLO 7

Independent Research and Learning

Undertake independent inquiry, particularly at the postgraduate level, and pursue continuous professional development.
